It validates closed vocabularies and owner/producer/denominator currentness against committed authorities. It does not consume live candidate receipts, execute falsifiers, aggregate evidence, or change release controllers.

negative_control_catalog.description: Public state changed during publish=false rehearsal.
Checksum-invalid or partial install is accepted as ready.
Public claim text differs from the reviewed catalog.
A duplicate or late terminal outcome is published after cancellation.
A known-false exact result is admitted as current.
Missing health evidence is represented as a specific repair diagnosis.
Not-ready is flattened to successful empty.
An old-generation result or effect is published as current.
Optional tools absent cause native product health to fail.
A partial or unsafe edit is authorized.
Process cleanup is omitted and an orphan remains.
A producer is removed while the count field remains and defaults clean.
Publisher authority is reachable during no-publish rehearsal.
Ranged input mutates last-good source under full-sync.
A required archive, SBOM, or attestation subject is omitted.
A server/DAP pair is partially promoted while UI reports ready.
Startup lifecycle evidence is omitted while providers appear to respond.
An installed-required contribution is only statically registered.
An unsupported architecture silently selects another target.
A workspace or PATH binary substitutes for the candidate.
